facts.text: Hilltop earned its name because it sits higher than the surrounding Denver neighborhoods, offering sweeping views of the Front Range.
The neighborhood began as a silver‑mining settlement in the 1880s, with prospectors flooding in after discoveries along Clear Creek.
A historic railroad, the Clear Creek & Boulder line, once linked Hilltop to Denver, sustaining the town until mining activity waned.
Hilltop’s early homes were simple log cabins and stone foundations, many of which survive in the neighborhood’s late‑19th‑century architecture.
Today, Hilltop balances outdoor recreation with historic preservation, as local groups work to stabilize old mine tailings and protect the area’s natural beauty.
Cranmer Park, located in Hilltop’s center, offers a popular spot for residents to enjoy mountain views and community events.
